# #1717: Patch: an account flooding the API raises the unusual-rejections alert
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

## What it actually means

When a match socket gets flooded with refused actions, the server raises an "unusual rejections" alert so abuse gets noticed. The ordinary web API enforces the same kind of per-account limits, but refused requests there are only logged one line at a time and never counted — an account can hammer the API indefinitely without the alert ever firing. After the change, sustained refusals at the API trip the same alert the socket side already raises.

## Why

Spec §9.8 says "every rejected action is logged with its reason, and accounts with an unusual rejection rate raise an alert." Only the socket side implements it: `SeatGuard::note_rejection` feeds `alert_unusual_rejections` → `match.rejections.unusual` (`crates/server/src/actor/guard.rs:73-105`). On the HTTP path each refusal is warn-logged (`api.rate_limited`, `crates/server/src/api/http.rs:1107-1115`) and rejected requests are deliberately unrecorded (:847-848); `log_alert` exists but is never used on this path. A persistently abusive account or address produces noise, not a signal.

## Proposal

Mirror the socket side: keep a bounded per-account/per-address window of refusals in the rate-limiter's state, and past a named threshold in `crates/server/src/config.rs` emit one `api.rejections.unusual` alert per window — same shape as `match.rejections.unusual` so existing alerting picks it up.

## Where it lands

`crates/server/src/api/http.rs` (`RateLimiterState`), `crates/server/src/config.rs` (the threshold and window, CLAUDE.md rule 9), tests in the server suite. Spec §9.8.

## Acceptance criteria

- Driving N refused requests inside the window raises exactly one `api.rejections.unusual` alert per window.
- Under the threshold, or spread past the window, nothing alerts.
- The window is bounded (no unbounded state per account), matching the guard's pattern.

## Size and risks

Small. Classed `security` because it is a missing §9.8 abuse mitigation rather than a bypass: without it the abuse surface's own tripwire never fires on the HTTP half of the API.
